title: Architecture and Trade-off Analysis
description: Weighing non-functional requirements against real constraints, writing architecture decision records that name and justify rejected alternatives, and defending a system-level design decision when a constraint changes.

levels.name: Foundation
levels.description: Can identify the non-functional requirements relevant to a given scenario and translate at least one into a measurable budget, such as a latency or availability target, with a stated source for the number.

levels.name: Apprentice
levels.description: Can write a complete architecture decision record for a real decision that names at least two rejected alternatives, each with a distinct stated reason, and at least one accepted negative consequence.

levels.name: Practitioner
levels.description: Can independently compare architectural styles or data-architecture options against explicit, scenario-specific criteria and defend the recommendation against a reviewer's counter-scenario without retreating to a general preference.

levels.name: Journeyman
levels.description: Can design for failure and degradation across a system boundary, and can revise a prior architecture decision when a stated constraint changes, explaining precisely what the new constraint invalidated.

levels.name: Mastery Evidence
levels.description: Can produce and defend an end-to-end architecture for a self-scoped, ambiguous problem in front of a mixed technical and non-technical panel, incorporating constraint changes raised live and revising the ADR set afterward.
